name: Charlie Health IOP vs Headway
title: Charlie Health IOP vs Headway: Intensive Care vs Outpatient Network
description: Compare Charlie Health's virtual IOP for teens/young adults with Headway's therapist credentialing network. Understand when intensive outpatient vs standard therapy is appropriate.

summary.bottom_line: Charlie Health and Headway serve completely different clinical needs. Charlie Health provides intensive outpatient programs (9-12 hours/week) for teens and young adults (ages 11-30) with serious mental health conditions. Headway helps therapists accept insurance for standard outpatient therapy. Choose based on clinical acuity - IOP for higher-need cases, Headway for standard weekly therapy.

sections.heading: Different Levels of Care
sections.content: Charlie Health and Headway address fundamentally different treatment needs. Charlie Health is a virtual intensive outpatient program providing 9-12 hours of weekly treatment for teens and young adults with serious mental health conditions including suicidal ideation, self-harm, and eating disorders. Headway is a platform helping therapists accept insurance for standard weekly outpatient therapy. These serve different points on the mental health care continuum.

sections.heading: When to Choose Each
sections.content: Charlie Health IOP is appropriate when weekly therapy isn't sufficient - for patients stepping down from inpatient care, experiencing crisis, or needing structured intensive treatment. The program includes individual therapy, group therapy (3x/week), and family sessions. Headway is appropriate when someone needs standard outpatient therapy (typically 1 session/week) and wants access to in-network therapists at affordable copays.

sections.heading: Care Continuum Decision
sections.content: The choice depends on clinical need:

recommendations.when: A teen or young adult (11-30) needs more than weekly therapy - crisis history, suicidal ideation, eating disorder, or stepping down from inpatient.
An adult or teen needs standard outpatient therapy for anxiety, depression, or general mental health support.
Starting with Charlie Health IOP then stepping down to outpatient therapy through a Headway provider.

faqs.q: Is Charlie Health more intensive than regular therapy?
faqs.a: Yes, significantly. Charlie Health provides 9-12 hours of treatment weekly (IOP level), compared to standard outpatient therapy through Headway therapists which is typically 1 hour/week. IOP is for more serious conditions.

faqs.q: Can I use Charlie Health for mild anxiety?
faqs.a: Charlie Health is designed for serious mental health conditions requiring intensive treatment. For mild to moderate anxiety, standard outpatient therapy through a Headway provider would be more appropriate.

faqs.q: Does Charlie Health work with adults over 30?
faqs.a: No, Charlie Health specializes in teens (11-17) and young adults (18-30). Adults over 30 should seek outpatient therapists through platforms like Headway.
